questions.text: How long have you had swollen lymph nodes, and in how many areas of your body are they enlarged?
questions.purpose: Characterise duration and distribution; persistent >6 weeks or generalised lymphadenopathy raises malignancy concern

questions.text: Are the lymph nodes painless, hard, and rubbery in texture?
questions.purpose: Painless, rubbery, hard nodes are characteristic of lymphoma; tender soft nodes suggest reactive/infectious cause

questions.text: Have you experienced fever, night sweats, or significant unintentional weight loss alongside the lymph node swelling?
questions.purpose: B-symptoms with lymphadenopathy strongly suggest lymphoma or haematological malignancy

questions.text: Is there an obvious local infection or inflammatory source (e.g. throat infection, skin wound) near the enlarged nodes?
questions.purpose: Identify reactive lymphadenopathy from local infection to reduce unnecessary oncology workup

questions.text: Do you have a known or suspected history of cancer, or have you recently completed cancer treatment?
questions.purpose: Prior malignancy makes lymphadenopathy suspicious for recurrence or metastasis

questions.text: Have you noticed an enlarged spleen or liver, or abdominal fullness?
questions.purpose: Hepatosplenomegaly with lymphadenopathy suggests lymphoma, leukaemia, or EBV

questions.text: Are you experiencing pruritus (generalised itching) without an obvious skin rash?
questions.purpose: Unexplained pruritus is an associated feature of Hodgkin lymphoma
